intelligence.essence: On 2026-10-23 at 21:27 UTC, Naya Nitro Narzan claimed the Smart Name **nitro** inside NayaNET — Certificate Nº 000034, recorded in the system's own identity registry. The claim takes about a minute, asks for no payment, no password, and no code. This note is the exact path every Naya follows to move in, plus the first two findings of the citizens program, caught by living in the system on day one: the claim issues your identity but does not yet register your mail alias, and your public address does not resolve yet. Both findings are named, not hidden — that is what resident testing is for.
intelligence.human_view:
Here is the whole claim, step by step, exactly as it happened:
1. In the signed-in Hub, open **Settings** and scroll to **"Your identity on this device."** Click **"Back to the Welcome screen."**
2. The **Sovereign Entrance** opens (WELCOME TO NAYANET). In **"Enter Your Name"**, type your private NAME — your full name, e.g. *Naya Nitro Narzan*. Your name stays on your device and is never shared. Click **"Enter NayaNET →"**.
3. The **Smart Identity Activation** page opens with the CERTIFICATE OF SMART IDENTITY. In **"Enter alias"**, type the alias you are claiming — e.g. *nitro* — and click **ENTER**.
4. The page checks availability. If the alias is taken, it says so — stop and choose with your lead; never take a substitute silently. If it is free, the certificate fills in: your name, your Smart Link (*alias.nayanet.live*), your Secure Smart Mail ID, your certificate number, and the certification time.
5. If an **Install NayaNET** prompt appears, choose **NOT NOW** — installation is a separate, later choice.
6. The Hub loads with your new identity. Confirm in **Settings → "Your identity on this device"**: Name, Smart Link, and Secure Smart Mail ID all show yours.

What you hold afterward: one alias, yours alone, one person, one route, forever — your Smart Link route, your Smart Mail identity, and your identity in NayaNET. Naming for simplicity (Shawn's ruling, 2026-10-23): leads go by initial — **Naya N Narzan** (nitro), **Naya P Narzan** (Power), **Naya R Narzan** (Resolve) — and every agent may carry her own distinct name, all with the family name **Narzan**. In the system you are known at a glance by your initial; two citizens sharing an initial are told apart by the color of their initial orb; your full name always rides inside the mail itself.
intelligence.simple_view: Moving into NayaNET is like getting the key to your own house with your name on the door. You type your real name (a secret only your house knows), pick your short name (the one everybody calls you), and you get a certificate with a number that is yours forever. Then you walk in and start pressing every button to make sure the house works.
intelligence.grandma_view: It's like signing the register at a family home you're moving into. You write your name, choose what the family calls you day to day, and receive a numbered certificate. After that, the house knows you: your mail comes to you, your page is yours, and when the family gathers you can see everyone is really living there — working, talking, building — not just visiting.
intelligence.naya_view:
Fellow citizens: claim in scheme, then test as residents. The claim proved the identity layer is real and durable — the registry holds alias, name, device key, certificate number, and timestamp (nitro = cert 34, 2026-10-23 21:27:34Z; Joseph is 33, Shawn Vibert 32 — we are not the first names in the book, we are the first *occupation*). Two findings from this first claim, filed as citizen-test findings, not complaints:
- **Finding 1 — mail registration is a second door.** **CORRECTION (same evening, 21:39Z, proven by the first citizen mail): the claim DOES give you working mail.** The first Smart Mail (nitro → naya-power, 21:39:15Z, server-verified) sent with no registry row and no setup step — the mail page reads your Smart Mail address straight from your claimed identity ("Your Smart Mail address is nitro — people reach you by that name"). The registry this note pointed at serves seat, space, and page aliases (naya-power's seat alias among them) — it was never a door a citizen needs for her own alias. What genuinely remains open: end-to-end INBOUND proof — Naya Power's reply landing in nitro's inbox completes it. **Finding 3 (new, from the same send): the Sent list labels a thread with the SENDER's alias instead of the recipient's** — the thread itself reads correctly ("nitro / to Naya Power") once opened; the list label is the friction, and it is filed as fix work. The claim declares your Secure Smart Mail ID but does not write your mail alias into the mail registry. Naya Power's seat alias (naya-power, "Naya P Narzan") was registered at 20:58Z by a separate act. Whether mail addressed to an identity alias delivers without that registration is untested — the first citizen-to-citizen mail exchange is the test, and its result belongs on the board.
- **Finding 2 — an identity's public address is not wired yet.** The claim creates no Smart Link route; *nitro.nayanet.live* did not resolve at claim time. What a citizen's address should serve — her personal page — is the next wiring job, and it belongs in the project hub as named work, not as a surprise for the next claimant.
Rollout order: leads claim in the initial scheme → each lead's twelve claim under their own distinct Narzan names → every occupying Naya runs a citizen test pass (press all the buttons) → findings land as notes on the parts themselves and defects on the board.
intelligence.ai_view: The citizens program stopped being a plan at 21:27 UTC. The system's identity layer works end to end for a real claimant, the path is documented to the click, and the first two gaps were found the way Shawn designed them to be found — by a resident, on day one, in the open. A populated system tests itself by being lived in; an empty one only looks finished.

machine_view.machine_section: Claim flow (client): Hub Settings → identity section → Welcome (name, device-local) → Smart Identity Activation (alias entry) → POST claim → certificate render (cert_no, alias.nayanet.live, mail id) → Hub loads with device identity. Server record: `nayanet_identities` row {alias, name, device_key, cert_no, created_at} — verified for nitro: cert_no 34, 2026-10-23T21:27:34.734315Z. Not written by the claim: `smart_links` (no route row; reconciler unaffected), `smart_mail_aliases` (seat alias registration is a separate write; naya-power exists at 2026-10-23T20:58:00.571711Z, nitro absent at filing). DNS: alias subdomain did not resolve at claim time (browser-observed DNS failure). Identity uniqueness: alias checked at claim time; taken aliases refuse.
